note: Clean gate pass with real caveats. validate_items.R --table-sets: item set 12/12 (SCPV1..SCPV12) and resp set 1-5 both exact. 60 rows shipped (12 items x 5 levels). (1) STEP 3b INSTRUMENT MISMATCH -- THE DICTIONARY DESCRIPTION IS WRONG AND SHOULD BE CORRECTED. The IRW dictionary row reads "Socio-Cognitive Profile Victimization scale (SCPV)" and the sibling processing script data/ren_2019_psychopathy_children.py comments SCPV as "Self-reported Child Psychopathy Version". Neither is the instrument. Ren et al. (2019)'s Measures section heads the block "Social Competence - Parents Version (SCPV)" and says: "Parents also completed the SCPV, as developed by the Conduct Problems Prevention Research Group (Conduct Problems Prevention Research Group [Cpprg], 1995). This scale consists of 12 items that assess a child's positive social behaviors, including emotion regulation, prosocial behaviors, and communication skills. Parents are asked to rate how well each of the twelve statements describes their child on a five-point Likert scale, from 1 (not at all) to 5 (very well)." It is the Fast Track Social Competence Scale - Parent Version, a parent report of prosocial competence -- not a victimization measure and not a psychopathy measure. The extraction follows the live data, and the instrument field says so. Flagged for the orchestrator; no row was written to pending_index_notes.csv from this agent. (2) ENGLISH FALLBACK. The 299 respondents were parents of Chinese schoolchildren in a Guangzhou-approved study, so the administered wording was Chinese; the paper never states a translation procedure for the SCPV specifically (it describes forward/back translation only for the YPI-CV). Recoverability is scoped to the deposit and the paper's own supplements, and neither holds any Chinese: the figshare deposit is a single .xlsx (299 x 88, sha256 0ebf515eed34cc02e729b9e32ffb48d1c609a098e1c458ec9c759050a0e73c6e) whose 88 headers are bare codes (ID, gender, age, EDUCATION, INCOME, YPIC1-18, CPTI1-28, SDQ1-25, SCPV1-12) with no variable labels and zero CJK characters, and the Frontiers article prints no item wording for any of its four instruments. So the CPPRG's own English ships in the base fields with language=Chinese and the _translated columns omitted (text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=official_instrument_english). (3) INSTRUCTIONS DELIBERATELY LEFT BLANK. The Fast Track form carries an instruction -- "I will read to you some statements that could describe your child. Please tell me how well each of the statements actually does describe your child." -- but it describes an interviewer-read administration, and Ren et al. administered the parent questionnaires as take-home paper forms ("Parental questionnaires and consent letters were placed in envelopes and taken home by the children. The parents were instructed to return the questionnaires in a sealed envelope to their teacher within 2 days."). Shipping it would assert framing text these respondents demonstrably did not receive, so instructions is blank rather than filled with a prompt from the wrong mode of administration. Ren et al. publish no instruction text of their own. section_prompt blank (single trivial section_id, no testlets); correct_response blank (no key, it is a rating scale). (4) OPTION ANCHORS ARE SHIFTED +1 FROM THE SOURCE FORM. The Fast Track form codes the five points 0-4 ("Not At All (0), A Little (1), Moderately Well (2), Well (3), Very Well (4)"); the IRW table stores 1-5, and Ren et al. state the scale as "a five-point Likert scale, from 1 (not at all) to 5 (very well)". Both endpoints therefore corroborate the alignment from the study's own text; the three middle anchors (A Little / Moderately Well / Well) are the CPPRG form's, carried over in order, and no level is padded with its own number. Anchors are transcribed with the form's own title-case capitalisation. (5) MAPPING. mapping_basis=reconstructed, status PARTIAL -- see verification_ren2019_scpv.csv and verify_ren2019_scpv.R. Code derivation is pattern 1 (the IRW item code IS the source column name: data/ren2019_psychopathy_children.py melts [c for c in df.columns if c.startswith('SCPV')] with var_name='item', no rename, no enumerate, no positional range), but that grants NO exemption here, because the source file carries no labels of any kind -- the tie between the code SCPVk and item k of the instrument rests entirely on the numeric suffix. Verified against data: the live per-item mean profile (rescaled to the form's 0-4 metric) tracks the Fast Track Grade 2/Year 3 technical report's published per-item means at Spearman 0.888 (normative sample) and 0.930 (control sample), Pearson 0.937, permutation p = 0.00015 over 20,000 random relabelings of the 12 codes. That rules out a permutation but not individual swaps: 30 of the 66 single swaps still clear Spearman 0.80, and three of them (SCPV1<->SCPV2, SCPV6<->SCPV11, SCPV6<->SCPV12) actually raise it to 0.902. Corroboration from Ren et al.'s own reported alphas is weak and reported as such: the CPPRG partition (emotion regulation 1,2,3,5,6,8; prosocial/communication 4,7,9,10,11,12) gives observed 0.742 / 0.870 against reported 0.78 / 0.88 (total 0.887 vs 0.90) and ranks 39th of the 924 possible 6/6 splits, i.e. consistent but not the closest. Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. (6) RIGHTS: no block. itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv has no row for this instrument (searched 'social competence', 'fast track', 'CPPRG', 'conduct problems' -- zero hits). The rights holder is the Conduct Problems Prevention Research Group / Duke University's Fast Track Project, and its own measure page (https://fasttrackproject.org/measure/social-competence-parent/) both posts the blank instrument as a free PDF and answers its own question "Is this Measure Available for Public Use?: Yes". No fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause is quotable from that page or from the technical reports; the only rights string on the page is the site footer "Copyright (c) 2026, Sanford School of Public Policy @ Duke University", which is a notice about the site, not a term about the instrument (the PANAS precedent). Silence is permission (irw#1945), so extraction proceeded. No register row was written -- a round may write a 'block' row but never a 'ship' row (Ben, 2026-09-10); this is a ship-shaped case and is escalated here rather than recorded.
